opening_message:
Ticket 1: John Rodriguez (employee ID E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E049.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: John Rodriguez (E049), Analyst, full-time. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the role (Engineer for Source Code), so write is the maximum. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows John Rodriguez (E049) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; contractors never get admin, and write requires advanced training. With only basic training, the maximum is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: HR lists John Rodriguez (E049) as full-time Analyst, while Security lists him as a contractor with basic security training. Under the contractor interpretation, the maximum access to Source Code (owned by the Engineer role) is read, since contractors never get admin and write requires advanced security training, which the Security note says he lacks (basic only). Since the requested write exceeds the contractor maximum, and the safer/conservative reading applies given the conflicting evidence, I grant read.
